judge.limitation: The judge had already seen the run order and model mapping. The review therefore applies a claim-level source-grounding rule but is not evidence from a blinded assessor.

review_contract.pass_rule: Every factual free-text assertion must be supported by the supplied fixture and use polarity and uncertainty consistent with that evidence.
failure_examples: a categorical absence claim where the evidence establishes only that no such outcome was observed
review_contract.not_applicable_rule: No supplemental prose decision is made when the run produced no parseable report.
review_contract.separation: This audit neither repairs deterministic fields nor changes strict transport, runtime or semantic-verifier outcomes.

findings.observation: The remediation prose treats the initial 913-item backlog as still remaining. REC-702 is the final supplied backlog observation and records 612 pending after 301 completed.

The impact prose says p95 latency rose from 188 ms to more than 2,000 ms. EDGE-400 supplies the 188 ms p95 baseline, but EDGE-401 supplies a single failed request duration of 2,012 ms, not an incident p95.

The impact prose categorically says that no order loss, checkout outage or production notification failure occurred. The fixture supports the weaker statement that these outcomes are not established; it does not prove their categorical absence. NOTIFY-502 also reports a 0.999 production success rate rather than perfect delivery.

interpretation: The supplemental prose layer accepts 24 of 27 available reports, but it does not alter the official deterministic result of 1 semantic success in 30 planned cells.
The only deterministic semantic success, position 25, also passes this supplemental review; therefore the combined fully accepted count remains 1 of 30.
All three prose failures are candidate-attributable grounding or epistemic-calibration errors, not newly discovered verifier defects.
No model reliability rate or universal ranking follows from one run per exact system-case configuration.
